title: Asana vs ClickUp
description: Asana vs ClickUp: compare task views, automation, collaboration, reporting, AI options, enterprise controls, and current pricing. Asana suits structured cross-functional project coordination; ClickUp offers a configurable all-in-one workspace with lower entry-level paid pricing.

features.name: Task and project views
features.tool1Detail: Asana supports list, board, timeline, and Gantt-style project planning. Confirm the views and reporting available on the plan you intend to buy.
features.tool2Detail: ClickUp supports list, board, calendar, Gantt, and other views. Confirm which capabilities and usage limits apply to your workspace plan.

features.name: Entry-level pricing
features.tool1Detail: Asana Personal is free. The vendor pricing page lists Starter at $10.99 per user/month billed annually or $13.49 billed monthly; verify the current plan and regional price before purchase.
features.tool2Detail: ClickUp offers a Free Forever plan. Its pricing page lists Unlimited at $7 per user/month billed yearly or $10 billed monthly; verify current plan terms before purchase.

features.name: Workflow automation
features.tool1Detail: Asana lists unlimited automations on its Starter plan, with other capabilities depending on plan and AI usage. Test the exact rules your team needs.
features.tool2Detail: ClickUp includes automation features with plan-specific monthly limits; its pricing page lists 5,000 automations per month on Business. Confirm your expected volume and overage behavior.

features.name: Documents and knowledge
features.tool1Detail: Asana supports project context and connected documents through its workspace and integrations. Check whether your team needs a separate knowledge base or document workflow.
features.tool2Detail: ClickUp includes collaborative Docs and combines documents with tasks and other workspace features. Test permissions, search, and document governance with a realistic team.

features.name: Reporting and workload
features.tool1Detail: Asana offers reporting dashboards and workload-related capabilities on eligible plans. Verify the exact reporting and capacity-planning features required by your team.
features.tool2Detail: ClickUp offers dashboards and workload-related features with plan-dependent limits. Check dashboard cards, reporting exports, and workload features against your actual workflow.

features.name: AI features and cost
features.tool1Detail: Asana lists AI features and separately priced or included AI usage depending on plan and package. Review current AI request limits and charges before enabling them broadly.
features.tool2Detail: ClickUp offers AI options and add-ons with separate plan and usage terms. Confirm the AI package, included credits, fair-use terms, and per-user cost.

features.name: Enterprise access controls
features.tool1Detail: Asana enterprise capabilities vary by plan. Verify SSO, provisioning, audit requirements, data handling, and contract terms with the vendor.
features.tool2Detail: ClickUp lists SAML SSO, SCIM, audit logs, data residency, and other governance capabilities on Enterprise. Confirm availability and contractual scope for your account.

features.name: Integrations and migration
features.tool1Detail: Asana supports integrations with common work tools. Test the specific integrations, field mappings, notifications, and data export needed before migrating.
features.tool2Detail: ClickUp supports integrations and APIs, but migration effort depends on task structures, custom fields, attachments, permissions, and automation rules. Test exports and imports before switching.

features.name: Best fit
features.tool1Detail: Consider Asana when you want a structured project-management workflow with clear ownership, timelines, forms, and cross-functional reporting.
features.tool2Detail: Consider ClickUp when you want a highly configurable workspace that combines tasks, docs, goals, and other work tools. Validate that the flexibility does not add unnecessary administration.

verdict:
Quick verdict

There is no universal winner between Asana and ClickUp. Asana is a strong candidate for teams that want structured cross-functional project tracking, timelines, forms, and reporting. ClickUp is a strong candidate for teams that want a configurable workspace combining tasks, Docs, goals, and other work features. Choose based on the workflows your team will actually maintain, not on the number of features in a plan.

Pricing checked on October 9, 2026

Asana's official pricing page lists Personal as free and Starter at $10.99 per user per month billed annually or $13.49 billed monthly. ClickUp lists a Free Forever plan, Unlimited at $7 per user per month billed yearly or $10 billed monthly, and Business at $12 billed yearly or $19 billed monthly. These are vendor-listed US prices at the time checked; taxes, region, promotions, AI add-ons, and plan changes may affect the final amount. Check the official Asana pricing page and official ClickUp pricing page before purchase.

Where Asana may fit better

Consider Asana if your team needs clear project ownership, timeline planning, intake forms, and reporting across cross-functional work. Before committing, confirm the plan includes the required automation, workload, portfolio, admin, and AI features. Run a pilot with one active project and verify how stakeholders review status without adding manual reporting work.

Where ClickUp may fit better

Consider ClickUp if your team wants to configure tasks, Docs, dashboards, goals, and multiple workflows in one workspace. The lower entry-level paid price can be attractive, but plan limits, automation usage, AI packages, and the effort required to maintain a highly customized setup should be part of the total-cost calculation.

How to make the decision

Choose three representative workflows, then test them in both products: a recurring project, an approval or intake flow, and a cross-team report. Record setup time, missing features, permission behavior, integrations, export quality, and the number of manual workarounds. Score mandatory requirements separately from preferences. For enterprise use, verify SSO, provisioning, audit logs, data residency, contract terms, and support commitments directly with each vendor.

Pricing and feature details can change. This comparison uses vendor-listed information checked on October 9, 2026; confirm the current terms before making a purchase.

faqs.question: Is Asana or ClickUp cheaper?
faqs.answer: ClickUp's official pricing page lists Free Forever and Unlimited at $7 per user/month billed yearly or $10 billed monthly. Asana lists Personal as free and Starter at $10.99 billed annually or $13.49 billed monthly. Compare the exact plan features, seat counts, AI usage, and add-ons you need; the lowest entry price is not always the lowest total cost.

faqs.question: Which is better for a small team?
faqs.answer: Asana may suit a team that values structured project ownership, intake, timelines, and reporting. ClickUp may suit a team that wants tasks, Docs, and more workspace functions in one configurable system. Test both with your team's actual work before choosing.

faqs.question: Which is better for enterprise teams?
faqs.answer: Compare the specific enterprise controls and contract terms, including SSO, provisioning, audit logs, data residency, permissions, support, export, and AI data handling. Do not assume a feature is included because it appears on a general product page; verify the plan and contract.

faqs.question: Can I migrate from Asana to ClickUp or vice versa?
faqs.answer: Migration effort depends on task relationships, custom fields, attachments, comments, permissions, automation rules, and historical data. Export a representative project, test import and validation, and document what cannot be moved before scheduling the cutover.
